tasks.title: Anatomy tour: every organ, one by one
tasks.prompt: Open the Anatomy tab and click each structure in turn: the viewer jumps to it and shows it alone. For each one, say which neighbours touch it, then scroll to its top and bottom.

hints.text: Use ‹ and › in the banner on the image to step through the structures in order.

tasks.explanation: Seeing each organ alone, then in context, builds the 3D map you need before looking for disease.

rubric.text: Visited every structure in the list
Named the neighbours of the liver, pancreas, kidneys and bladder
Found the top and bottom slice of at least three organs

tasks.title: Name the solid organs
tasks.prompt: With named arrows, mark: liver, spleen, right kidney, left kidney, pancreas, gallbladder.

hints.text: Soft-tissue window. The liver is on the patient's right — the left of the screen.
The pancreas lies in front of the splenic vein; the gallbladder hangs under the liver.
Reveal.

tasks.explanation: One-to-one matching against the expert outlines; identity and side are graded separately from position.

tasks.title: Find the pancreas

hints.text: Jumping to a slice with the reference.
Reveal.

tasks.explanation: Graded against the expert outline from the source dataset; a point outside it is reported with its distance.

tasks.title: Classify the radiograph
tasks.prompt: Read the radiograph and choose the category the expert readers would assign for COVID-19 pneumonia.

options.why: Typical: multifocal, bilateral, peripheral and lower-zone predominant opacities.
Indeterminate: opacities present but without the typical distribution (e.g. unilateral, central or upper-zone).
Atypical: findings that point elsewhere — lobar consolidation, a solitary nodule or mass, cavitation, pleural effusion or pneumothorax.
Negative: no lung opacity.

hints.text: Divide each lung into upper, middle and lower zones and inner and outer halves; where are the opacities?

tasks.explanation: All three reader groups chose this category. Typical: multifocal, bilateral, peripheral and lower-zone predominant opacities.

tasks.title: How much lung is involved?
tasks.prompt: Count the lung zones with opacity (three per lung) and choose the extent.

options.why: Mild (1–2 lung zones). The readers counted zones on the frontal film.
Moderate (3–4 lung zones). The readers counted zones on the frontal film.
Severe (more than 4 lung zones). The readers counted zones on the frontal film.

hints.text: Zones: upper, middle and lower on each side — six in total.

tasks.explanation: Extent is counted in zones; it tracks severity and change over time better than a single word.

tasks.title: Judge the technical quality
tasks.prompt: Before reading the lungs, assess this frontal radiograph's technique: projection, inspiration (count posterior ribs), rotation (spinous processes vs clavicle heads) and penetration.

hints.text: A good inspiration shows about 9–10 posterior ribs above the diaphragm; rotation shifts the spinous processes away from the midpoint between the clavicle heads.

tasks.explanation: Technique changes appearances: poor inspiration crowds the bases and widens the heart; rotation distorts the mediastinum; AP projection magnifies the heart.

rubric.text: Projection stated (AP — heart size not reliable)
Inspiration judged by counting posterior ribs
Rotation judged with spinous processes and clavicle heads
Penetration judged (spine visible through the heart?)

tasks.explanation: No anatomical reference outlines exist for this radiograph, so compare your arrows with the book's figure of the normal contours and self-review.

rubric.text: Right border: SVC and right atrium identified
Left border: aortic knob, main pulmonary artery and left ventricle identified
Commented on whether any segment bulges or is effaced

tasks.title: Measure the cardiothoracic ratio
tasks.prompt: Use the Length tool (L) to measure the widest heart diameter and the widest inner thoracic diameter, then state the ratio and whether this projection allows a judgement of heart size.

hints.text: Measure the heart from its rightmost to leftmost point; the thorax at its widest inner rib margins, usually at the domes of the diaphragm.

tasks.explanation: The ratio is a heuristic for PA films; on AP films the heart is magnified, so an apparently large ratio is not reliable. Detector-plane pixel spacing is not patient-calibrated, but a ratio cancels that scale.

rubric.text: Both widths measured at the right places
Ratio stated
Projection caveat stated (PA: usable)

tasks.title: Name five structures
tasks.prompt: With named arrows, mark: heart, esophagus, spinal cord, right lung and left lung (any slices).

hints.text: Mediastinal window for heart, esophagus and cord; lung window for the lungs.
Reveal.

tasks.explanation: One-to-one matching against the expert outlines; identity and side are graded separately from position.

hints.text: Jumping to a slice with the reference.
